key_insight: A residual-driven adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin FEM provably reduces both its error estimator and true approximation error to zero under the stated assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The method supports reliable finite element simulation of elliptic problems with uncertain material coefficients represented by countably many parameters.
method: Construct a computable residual-based error estimator under a parametric saturation assumption.
Enforce K-compatibility so coupled finite element meshes have comparable mesh sizes.
Establish estimator reliability, K-dependent stability and reduction, and adaptive convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence proofs and numerical experiments that illustrate and confirm the theoretical findings.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on parametric saturation, while enforcing K-compatible meshes introduces a constraint on adaptive refinement.
paper_title: Convergence of an adaptive multilevel stochastic Galerkin FEM driven by a residual-based error estimator
